1→﻿# RustRide - Claude Code Context
     2→
     3→## Project Overview
     4→
     5→RustRide is an open-source, self-hosted indoor cycling training application built in Rust. It provides BLE sensor connectivity (smart trainers, power meters, HR monitors), structured workout execution with ERG mode control, real-time metrics display, ride recording, and export to standard formats (.fit, .tcx).
     6→
     7→## Technology Stack
     8→
     9→| Component | Technology |
    10→|-----------|------------|
    11→| Language | Rust stable (1.75+) |
    12→| GUI Framework | egui + eframe (0.33+) |
    13→| Accessibility | accesskit (built into eframe) |
    14→| BLE Communication | btleplug |
    15→| Audio | rodio |
    16→| Voice Control | vosk (optional feature) |
    17→| Async Runtime | tokio |
    18→| Database | SQLite via rusqlite |
    19→| Configuration | TOML via toml crate |
    20→| Internationalization | fluent, fluent-langneg, unic-langid |
    21→| Theme Detection | dark-light |
    22→| Logging | tracing |
    23→| Serialization | serde |
    24→
    25→## Project Structure
    26→
    27→```
    28→src/
    29→├── main.rs              # Application entry point
    30→├── app.rs               # egui application state
    31→├── lib.rs               # Library exports
    32→├── accessibility/       # Accessibility features (WCAG 2.1 AA/AAA)
    33→│   ├── colorblind.rs    # Colorblind-safe palettes
    34→│   ├── focus.rs         # Keyboard focus management
    35→│   ├── high_contrast.rs # High contrast mode
    36→│   ├── screen_reader.rs # Screen reader support (accesskit)
    37→│   └── voice_control.rs # Voice control (optional Vosk feature)
    38→├── audio/               # Audio system (rodio)
    39→│   ├── engine.rs        # Audio engine
    40→│   └── tones.rs         # Tone generation for cues
    41→├── i18n/                # Internationalization (fluent)
    42→├── input/               # Input handling
    43→│   ├── keyboard.rs      # Keyboard shortcuts
    44→│   ├── touch.rs         # Touch input
    45→│   └── gestures.rs      # Gesture recognition
    46→├── onboarding/          # First-run onboarding wizard
    47→├── sensors/             # BLE/ANT+ sensor management
    48→├── workouts/            # Workout parsing and execution
    49→├── recording/           # Ride recording and file export
    50→├── metrics/             # Training metric calculations
    51→├── storage/             # SQLite and config persistence
    52→└── ui/                  # egui screens and widgets
    53→    ├── screens/         # Main application screens
    54→    ├── widgets/         # Reusable UI components
    55→    ├── display_modes/   # Flow mode, TV mode
    56→    ├── layout/          # Widget layout management
    57→    └── theme.rs         # Theme detection and management
    58→
    59→tests/
    60→├── unit/               # Unit tests
    61→├── integration/        # Integration tests
    62→└── fixtures/           # Test data (workouts, rides)
    63→
    64→specs/                  # Feature specifications
    65→├── 001-indoor-cycling-app/  # MVP cycling features
    66→├── 008-ux-accessibility/    # UX & Accessibility features
    67→│   ├── spec.md         # Feature specification
    68→│   ├── plan.md         # Implementation plan
    69→│   └── tasks.md        # Implementation tasks
    70→```
    71→
    72→## Key Modules
    73→
    74→### sensors/
    75→BLE sensor discovery and connection using btleplug. Supports:
    76→- FTMS (Fitness Machine Service) for smart trainers
    77→- Cycling Power Service for power meters
    78→- Heart Rate Service for HR monitors
    79→
    80→### workouts/
    81→Workout file parsing (.zwo, .mrc) and execution engine. Manages:
    82→- Workout state machine (start, pause, resume, skip)
    83→- ERG mode power target calculations
    84→- Interval timing and transitions
    85→
    86→### recording/
    87→Ride data capture and export. Features:
    88→- 1-second sample recording
    89→- Auto-save for crash recovery (30-second intervals)
    90→- Export to TCX, FIT, GPX, CSV formats
    91→
    92→### metrics/
    93→Training metric calculations:
    94→- Normalized Power (NP)
    95→- Training Stress Score (TSS)
    96→- Intensity Factor (IF)
    97→- Power and HR zone calculations
    98→
    99→### storage/
   100→Data persistence:
   101→- SQLite for rides, workouts, sensors
   102→- TOML for user configuration
   103→- Auto-migrations on startup
   104→
   105→## Development Commands
   106→
   107→```bash
   108→# Build
   109→cargo build              # Debug build
   110→cargo build --release    # Release build
   111→
   112→# Test
   113→cargo test               # Run all tests
   114→cargo test sensors       # Test specific module
   115→
   116→# Run
   117→cargo run                # Debug mode
   118→cargo run --release      # Release mode
   119→
   120→# Code quality
   121→cargo fmt                # Format code
   122→cargo clippy             # Lint
   123→```
   124→
   125→## Important Patterns
   126→
   127→### Thread Communication
   128→- Use `crossbeam::channel` for sensor data (BLE → UI)
   129→- Use `Arc<Mutex<T>>` for shared state (ride samples)
   130→- Call `ctx.request_repaint()` from background threads to wake UI
   131→
   132→### BLE Protocol
   133→- FTMS Control Point writes for ERG mode: `[0x05, watts_lo, watts_hi]`
   134→- Always request control (`[0x00]`) before setting targets
   135→- Handle automatic reconnection on signal loss
   136→
   137→### Metrics Calculations
   138→- Normalized Power: 30s rolling average → 4th power → mean → 4th root
   139→- TSS = (hours × IF²) × 100
   140→- Filter power spikes > 2000W as noise
   141→
   142→## Configuration Locations
   143→
   144→- **Windows**: `%APPDATA%\rustride\`
   145→- **macOS**: `~/Library/Application Support/rustride/`
   146→- **Linux**: `~/.config/rustride/` (config), `~/.local/share/rustride/` (data)
   147→
   148→## Accessibility Features
   149→
   150→The application follows WCAG 2.1 AA/AAA guidelines:
   151→
   152→### Keyboard Navigation
   153→- Tab/Shift+Tab for focus navigation
   154→- Enter/Space for button activation
   155→- Escape to close modals
   156→- F1/? to show keyboard shortcuts overlay
   157→- Ctrl+M for screen reader metrics announcement
   158→
   159→### Visual Accessibility
   160→- High contrast mode (7:1 WCAG AAA ratio)
   161→- Colorblind-safe palettes (deuteranopia, protanopia, tritanopia)
   162→- System theme detection and follow (dark/light)
   163→- Minimum 44x44px touch targets
   164→
   165→### Screen Reader Support
   166→- AccessKit integration (NVDA, VoiceOver, Orca)
   167→- Live regions for interval changes
   168→- Immediate alert announcements
   169→- Focus management for modal dialogs
   170→
   171→### Voice Control (optional)
   172→Enable with `--features voice-control`:
   173→- Commands: start, pause, resume, end, skip
   174→- Increase/decrease power targets
   175→- Status announcements
   176→
   177→### Touch/Gesture Support
   178→- Swipe navigation between screens
   179→- Pinch-zoom for charts
   180→- 44x44 minimum touch targets
   181→- Visual touch feedback (ripple/scale/highlight)
   182→
   183→## Current Feature: 001-indoor-cycling-app
   184→
   185→MVP implementation covering:
   186→- P1: Connect smart trainer and start free ride
   187→- P2: Execute structured workouts with ERG mode
   188→- P3: Record and export ride data
   189→- P4: Real-time training metrics display
   190→- P5: User profile and training zones
   191→- P6: Ride history browsing
   192→- P7: Multi-sensor support
   193→
   194→See `specs/001-indoor-cycling-app/` for full specifications.
   195→

1→//! Fitness Platform Sync
     2→//!
     3→//! Provides OAuth authentication and activity upload to fitness platforms.
     4→
     5→pub mod garmin;
     6→pub mod oauth;
     7→pub mod service;
     8→pub mod strava;
     9→
    10→use chrono::{DateTime, Utc};
    11→use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
    12→use std::collections::HashMap;
    13→use thiserror::Error;
    14→use uuid::Uuid;
    15→
    16→// Re-export main types
    17→pub use oauth::{CallbackResult, CredentialStore, OAuthCallbackServer, OAuthHandler};
    18→pub use service::{
    19→    create_sync_service, create_sync_service_with_db, PlatformStatus, SyncEvent, SyncMessage,
    20→    SyncService, SyncServiceHandle, UploadQueueEntry,
    21→};
    22→
    23→/// Sync-related errors
    24→#[derive(Debug, Error)]
    25→pub enum SyncError {
    26→    #[error("Platform not configured: {0:?}")]
    27→    NotConfigured(SyncPlatform),
    28→
    29→    #[error("Authorization required")]
    30→    AuthorizationRequired,
    31→
    32→    #[error("Token expired")]
    33→    TokenExpired,
    34→
    35→    #[error("Token refresh failed: {0}")]
    36→    RefreshFailed(String),
    37→
    38→    #[error("Upload failed: {0}")]
    39→    UploadFailed(String),
    40→
    41→    #[error("API error: {0}")]
    42→    ApiError(String),
    43→
    44→    #[error("Credential storage error: {0}")]
    45→    CredentialError(String),
    46→
    47→    #[error("Network error: {0}")]
    48→    NetworkError(String),
    49→
    50→    #[error("Activity already exists on {0:?}")]
    51→    DuplicateActivity(SyncPlatform),
    52→
    53→    #[error("Invalid FIT file: {0}")]
    54→    InvalidFitFile(String),
    55→
    56→    #[error("Request timed out after {0} seconds")]
    57→    Timeout(u64),
    58→
    59→    #[error("Rate limit exceeded. Please try again later.")]
    60→    RateLimited,
    61→}
    62→
    63→/// Supported sync platforms
    64→#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Serialize, Deserialize)]
    65→pub enum SyncPlatform {
    66→    /// Garmin Connect
    67→    GarminConnect,
    68→    /// Strava
    69→    Strava,
    70→    /// Apple Health (macOS only)
    71→    #[cfg(target_os = "macos")]
    72→    HealthKit,
    73→    /// TrainingPeaks
    74→    TrainingPeaks,
    75→    /// Intervals.icu
    76→    IntervalsIcu,
    77→}
    78→
    79→impl SyncPlatform {
    80→    /// Get display name
    81→    pub fn display_name(&self) -> &'static str {
    82→        match self {
    83→            SyncPlatform::GarminConnect => "Garmin Connect",
    84→            SyncPlatform::Strava => "Strava",
    85→            #[cfg(target_os = "macos")]
    86→            SyncPlatform::HealthKit => "Apple Health",
    87→            SyncPlatform::TrainingPeaks => "TrainingPeaks",
    88→            SyncPlatform::IntervalsIcu => "Intervals.icu",
    89→        }
    90→    }
    91→
    92→    /// Get authorization URL base
    93→    pub fn auth_url_base(&self) -> &'static str {
    94→        match self {
    95→            SyncPlatform::GarminConnect => "https://connect.garmin.com/oauthConfirm",
    96→            SyncPlatform::Strava => "https://www.strava.com/oauth/authorize",
    97→            #[cfg(target_os = "macos")]
    98→            SyncPlatform::HealthKit => "", // No OAuth for HealthKit
    99→            SyncPlatform::TrainingPeaks => "https://oauth.trainingpeaks.com/OAuth/Authorize",
   100→            SyncPlatform::IntervalsIcu => "https://intervals.icu/oauth/authorize",
   101→        }
   102→    }
   103→
   104→    /// Check if platform uses OAuth
   105→    pub fn uses_oauth(&self) -> bool {
   106→        match self {
   107→            #[cfg(target_os = "macos")]
   108→            SyncPlatform::HealthKit => false,
   109→            _ => true,
   110→        }
   111→    }
   112→}
   113→
   114→/// Sync configuration
   115→#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
   116→pub struct SyncConfig {
   117→    /// Platform-specific configurations
   118→    pub platforms: HashMap<SyncPlatform, PlatformConfig>,
   119→}
   120→
   121→impl Default for SyncConfig {
   122→    fn default() -> Self {
   123→        let mut platforms = HashMap::new();
   124→
   125→        platforms.insert(SyncPlatform::GarminConnect, PlatformConfig::default());
   126→        platforms.insert(SyncPlatform::Strava, PlatformConfig::default());
   127→        platforms.insert(SyncPlatform::TrainingPeaks, PlatformConfig::default());
   128→        platforms.insert(SyncPlatform::IntervalsIcu, PlatformConfig::default());
   129→
   130→        Self { platforms }
   131→    }
   132→}
   133→
   134→/// Platform-specific configuration
   135→#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, Default)]
   136→pub struct PlatformConfig {
   137→    /// Whether this platform is enabled
   138→    pub enabled: bool,
   139→    /// Auto-sync after ride completion
   140→    pub auto_sync: bool,
   141→}
   142→
   143→/// Sync record for tracking upload status
   144→#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
   145→pub struct SyncRecord {
   146→    /// Unique ID
   147→    pub id: Uuid,
   148→    /// Ride ID
   149→    pub ride_id: Uuid,
   150→    /// Target platform
   151→    pub platform: SyncPlatform,
   152→    /// Current status
   153→    pub status: SyncRecordStatus,
   154→    /// External activity ID (from platform)
   155→    pub external_id: Option<String>,
   156→    /// External activity URL
   157→    pub external_url: Option<String>,
   158→    /// When sync was initiated
   159→    pub created_at: DateTime<Utc>,
   160→    /// When sync completed
   161→    pub completed_at: Option<DateTime<Utc>>,
   162→    /// Error message if failed
   163→    pub error_message: Option<String>,
   164→    /// Number of retry attempts
   165→    pub retry_count: u32,
   166→}
   167→
   168→/// Sync record status
   169→#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
   170→pub enum SyncRecordStatus {
   171→    /// Pending upload
   172→    Pending,
   173→    /// Currently uploading
   174→    Uploading,
   175→    /// Upload completed successfully
   176→    Completed,
   177→    /// Upload failed
   178→    Failed,
   179→    /// Cancelled by user
   180→    Cancelled,
   181→}
   182→
   183→/// Trait for uploading to platforms
   184→pub trait PlatformUploader: Send + Sync {
   185→    /// Upload a ride to platform
   186→    fn upload(
   187→        &self,
   188→        platform: SyncPlatform,
   189→        ride_id: &Uuid,
   190→        fit_data: &[u8],
   191→    ) -> impl std::future::Future<Output = Result<SyncRecord, SyncError>> + Send;
   192→
   193→    /// Get upload status
   194→    fn get_status(&self, record_id: &Uuid) -> Option<SyncRecordStatus>;
   195→
   196→    /// Retry failed upload
   197→    fn retry(
   198→        &self,
   199→        record_id: &Uuid,
   200→    ) -> impl std::future::Future<Output = Result<SyncRecord, SyncError>> + Send;
   201→
   202→    /// Get sync history for a ride
   203→    fn get_sync_history(&self, ride_id: &Uuid) -> Vec<SyncRecord>;
   204→
   205→    /// Cancel pending upload
   206→    fn cancel(&self, record_id: &Uuid) -> bool;
   207→}
   208→
   209→#[cfg(test)]
   210→mod tests {
   211→    use super::*;
   212→
   213→    #[test]
   214→    fn test_platform_display_names() {
   215→        assert_eq!(SyncPlatform::Strava.display_name(), "Strava");
   216→        assert_eq!(SyncPlatform::GarminConnect.display_name(), "Garmin Connect");
   217→    }
   218→
   219→    #[test]
   220→    fn test_config_default() {
   221→        let config = SyncConfig::default();
   222→        assert!(config.platforms.contains_key(&SyncPlatform::Strava));
   223→        assert!(!config.platforms.get(&SyncPlatform::Strava).unwrap().enabled);
   224→    }
   225→}

     2→  "feature": "TrainingPeaks Sync",
     3→  "description": "# TrainingPeaks Sync

Add TrainingPeaks OAuth integration for uploading completed rides and downloading structured workout plans. Support both manual and automatic sync options.

## Rationale
TrainingPeaks is widely used by coached athletes and provides advanced training analytics. Supporting TrainingPeaks sync makes RustRide viable for serious athletes working with coaches, competing directly with TrainerRoad's value proposition.

## User Stories
- As a coached athlete, I want my rides to sync to TrainingPeaks so that my coach can see my training
- As a TrainingPeaks user, I want to download my workout plans so that I can execute them in RustRide

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] User can connect TrainingPeaks account via OAuth
- [ ] Completed rides upload to TrainingPeaks
- [ ] Workout plans can be downloaded from TrainingPeaks
- [ ] Downloaded workouts appear in workout library
- [ ] Sync status shown in UI

   484→            .send()
   485→            .await
   486→            .map_err(|e| SyncError::NetworkError(format!("Failed to send token request: {}", e)))?;

## ✅ Subtask T002 Completed

I've successfully implemented TrainingPeaks-specific OAuth token exchange and refresh logic in the `DefaultOAuthHandler`. Here's a summary of what was done:

### Changes Made to `src/integrations/sync/oauth.rs`:

1. **New Types Added:**
   - `TrainingPeaksTokenResponse` - Parses OAuth2 token responses with `expires_in` (seconds)
   - `TrainingPeaksOAuthErrorResponse` - Handles OAuth2 error format with `error`/`error_description`

2. **Handler Updates:**
   - Added `trainingpeaks_token_url` field to `DefaultOAuthHandler`
   - Added `TRAININGPEAKS_TOKEN_URL` constant (`https://oauth.trainingpeaks.com/oauth/token`)
   - Added `with_token_urls()` test helper for mocking both platforms

3. **New Methods:**
   - `exchange_trainingpeaks_token()` - Exchanges auth code for tokens
     - Includes `redirect_uri` in request (required by TrainingPeaks)
     - Converts `expires_in` to `DateTime<Utc>`
   - `refresh_trainingpeaks_token()` - Refreshes expired tokens
     - Detects `invalid_grant`/`invalid_token` requiring re-auth

4. **Switch Statements Updated:**
   - Added `SyncPlatform::TrainingPeaks` to `handle_callback` match
   - Added `SyncPlatform::TrainingPeaks` to `refresh_token` match

   - Token exchange: success, invalid code, server error
   - Token refresh: success, invalid grant (requires reauth), generic error

   157→    /// Validate FIT file data before upload.

   159→    /// Checks:

   163→    ///
   164→    /// # Arguments
   165→    /// * `fit_data` - The FIT file bytes

   167→    /// # Returns
   168→    /// Ok(()) if valid, or InvalidFitFile error with description
   169→    pub fn validate_fit_file(fit_data: &[u8]) -> Result<(), SyncError> {
   170→        // Check minimum size (header must be at least 12 bytes for basic FIT)
   171→        if fit_data.len() < 12 {
   172→            return Err(SyncError::InvalidFitFile(format!(
   173→                "File too small: {} bytes (minimum 12 bytes required)",
   174→                fit_data.len()
   175→            )));
   176→        }
   177→
   178→        // Check header size byte (first byte)
   179→        let header_size = fit_data[0];
   180→        if header_size != 12 && header_size != FIT_HEADER_SIZE {
   181→            return Err(SyncError::InvalidFitFile(format!(
   182→                "Invalid header size: {} (expected 12 or 14)",
   183→                header_size
   184→            )));
   185→        }
   186→
   187→        // Check FIT signature at bytes 8-11
   188→        if fit_data.len() >= 12 {
   189→            let signature = &fit_data[8..12];
   190→            if signature != FIT_HEADER_SIGNATURE {
   191→                return Err(SyncError::InvalidFitFile(
   192→                    "Missing '.FIT' signature in header".to_string(),
   193→                ));
   194→            }
   195→        }
   196→
   197→        // Check total file size is reasonable (at least header + some data)

   200→            return Err(SyncError::InvalidFitFile(format!(
   201→                "File truncated: {} bytes (expected at least {})",
   202→                fit_data.len(),
   203→                min_expected_size

   205→        }
   206→

5. **SyncService integration** - `process_single_upload()` handles duplicates specially by marking as completed (not failed)
6. **User-friendly message** - `get_user_friendly_error_message()` provides a clear duplicate message
7. **Comprehensive tests** - Including HTTP mocked tests for duplicate detection

**T010 Implementation Complete!** 

## Summary

Successfully implemented TrainingPeaks workout API types and conversion to internal workout formats:

### Changes Made

**1. `src/integrations/sync/trainingpeaks.rs`**
- Added imports for workout types (`CadenceTarget`, `PowerTarget`, `SegmentType`, `Workout`, `WorkoutFormat`, `WorkoutSegment`)
- Added `WorkoutConversionError` struct for error handling
- Implemented `TPWorkout::to_workout(ftp)` - main conversion method
- Added helper methods:
  - `convert_structure_to_segments()` - handles structured workouts or fallback to total_time
  - `convert_step_to_segments()` - recursively handles nested repeat steps  
  - `step_to_segment()` - converts single step to WorkoutSegment
  - `extract_power_target()` - handles Power targets (absolute watts or %FTP)
  - `extract_cadence_target()` - extracts Cadence targets
- Added `map_step_type_to_segment_type()` function
- Added `convert_tp_workouts()` batch conversion helper
- Added 13 comprehensive unit tests covering all conversion scenarios

**2. `src/workouts/types.rs`**
- Added `TrainingPeaks` variant to `WorkoutFormat` enum (completing T015 early)

### Key Features
- Handles structured workouts with multiple steps
- Supports nested repeat steps (e.g., 5x3min intervals)
- Converts power targets (absolute watts or percentage of FTP)
- Extracts cadence targets
- Falls back to total_time when no structure available
- Uses IF (Intensity Factor) to estimate power when available
- Proper error handling for invalid workouts

### Commit

### Summary of Changes

**New Features Added to `src/integrations/sync/trainingpeaks.rs`:**

1. **Power Zone Support (Coggan zones)**
   - `power_zone_to_percent_range()` - Maps Zone 1-7 to FTP percentage ranges
   - `parse_power_zone()` - Parses zone strings ("Zone 3", "Z3", "3")
   - Handles `PowerZone` target type from TrainingPeaks API

2. **Range Power Targets for Ramps**
   - `segment_type_uses_range_power()` - Identifies warmup/cooldown/ramp segments
   - `default_power_for_segment()` - Provides default Range targets:
     - Warmup: 40% → 75% FTP
     - Cooldown: 65% → 40% FTP
     - Ramp: 50% → 100% FTP

3. **Enhanced Power Target Extraction**
   - `extract_power_zone_target()` - Converts PowerZone to FTP %
   - `extract_power_value_target()` - Handles ranges for warmup/cooldown/ramp with min→max power

4. **Comprehensive Tests (11 new tests)**
   - Zone range mapping, zone parsing
   - Warmup/cooldown Range target defaults
   - Explicit range targets, zone-based intervals/ramps

    82→            PowerTarget::PercentFtp { percent } => (ftp as f32 * *percent as f32 / 100.0) as u16,
    83→            PowerTarget::Range { start, .. } => start.to_watts(ftp),

    88→    pub fn to_watts_at(&self, ftp: u16, progress: f32) -> u16 {
    89→        match self {

    97→            }

## T014 - TrainingPeaksSyncManager Implementation Complete ✅

### New Types Added to `src/integrations/sync/trainingpeaks.rs`:

1. **`WorkoutSyncConfig`** - Configuration for sync behavior:
   - `lookahead_days` (default: 14) - Days to look ahead for scheduled workouts
   - `lookback_days` (default: 7) - Days to look back
   - `ftp` - User's FTP for power target calculations
   - `auto_sync_enabled` - Whether to sync automatically
   - `sync_interval_hours` (default: 6) - Auto-sync interval
   - `cycling_only` - Filter to only sync cycling workouts

2. **`WorkoutSyncResult`** - Statistics from a sync operation:
   - Counts: fetched, converted, new, updated, skipped, errors
   - `synced_at` timestamp
   - Error messages for failed conversions

3. **`ImportedWorkout`** - Wrapper with TrainingPeaks metadata:
   - `workout` - The converted internal Workout
   - `external_id` - TrainingPeaks workout ID for sync tracking
   - `scheduled_date` - When the workout is scheduled
   - `planned_tss` / `planned_if` - Training metrics from the plan

4. **`TrainingPeaksSyncManager`** - Core manager with methods:
   - `sync_workouts()` - Fetch and convert workouts for configured date range
   - `sync_workouts_for_range()` - Sync for a custom date range
   - `get_workout()` - Fetch a single workout by ID
   - `is_sync_due()` - Check if auto-sync interval has elapsed
   - `mark_synced()` / `is_synced()` / `load_synced_ids()` - Track synced workouts

### Key Features:
- All imported workouts are marked with `WorkoutFormat::TrainingPeaks` source
- Non-cycling workouts (Run, Swim, etc.) are automatically filtered when `cycling_only` is enabled
- Synced workout IDs are tracked to distinguish new vs already-synced workouts
- Comprehensive error handling with detailed sync statistics

### Tests Added:
- 25+ unit tests covering config defaults, builder pattern, result tracking
- Manager creation and state management tests
- HTTP-mocked integration tests for sync operations

I've successfully implemented **T016: Store TrainingPeaks workouts in database** with the following changes:

     - `get_all_synced_workouts()` - lists all synced TP workouts
     - `get_sync_records()` - gets sync tracking records
     - `count_synced()` / `delete_synced_workout()` / `clear_all_synced()`

### Key Features
- Uses `ON CONFLICT` for upsert behavior on re-sync (updates existing workouts)
- Foreign key relationship between sync table and workouts table
- Efficient indexed lookups by external ID and scheduled date

    36→impl SyncRecordStatus {
